# DOC001: undocumented-public-item

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| family | DOC |
| product | frob |
| severity (default) | warn |
| tier | universal |
| scope | file |
| fix | manual |
| version | 1 |
| since | 2.0.0 |

A public item has no doc comment.

A doc comment is `///` or `/** */` directly above the item, or a `#[doc]`
attribute. Public items of test files, trait-impl members and file-backed
modules are not checked. This complements the compiler lint `missing_docs`
for languages without one.

## Examples

### DOC001 undocumented public items / Fires on a public function and a public struct #1 (line 6) (fire)

```rust
pub fn bare() {} // warn: DOC001
/// Documented.
pub struct Documented; 
pub struct Bare; // warn: DOC001
```

### DOC001 undocumented public items / Clean when documented or not public #2 (line 15) (clean)

```rust
/// Documented.
pub fn documented() {}

#[doc = "Documented by attribute."]
pub fn by_attribute() {}

/// Documented, with an attribute between.
#[inline]
pub fn with_attribute() {}

fn private() {}

pub(crate) fn crate_visible() {}

/// A type.
pub struct T;

impl std::fmt::Display for T {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result { f.write_str("t") }
}
```
